input.quote: (iv) Transition. Each Party shall use Diligent Efforts to cooperate with the other and/or its designee to effect a smooth and orderly transition in the Development, sale and ongoing marketing, promotion and commercialization of the Product in the Ono Territory during the Wind-down Period and to conduct in an expeditious manner any activities to be conducted under this Section 14.2.
input.rationale: A usable exit/transition regime exists and survives termination, so the rule is satisfied. Section 14.2(a)(iv) is expressly mutual ("Each Party shall use Diligent Efforts to cooperate with the other ... to effect a smooth and orderly transition ... during the Wind-down Period"), and Article XIV in its entirety survives under Section 14.5, so the cooperation obligation runs against Array as well as us. The Wind-down Period in 14.2(a)(ii) gives a defined, bracketed transition runway keyed to the termination ground, 14.2(a)(iii) and (vi) set out orderly transfer of Regulatory Filings, Data and materials with defined outside dates (assignment consistent with Wind-down obligations; return of materials within ninety (90) days), and cost allocation is expressly addressed in 14.2(a)(i) and (iii) rather than left as an open fee exposure, which answers the planner's concern about assistance being conditioned on extra fees. This is an in-licence, not a hosted service: there is no vendor-held "Customer Data" to export, and by design the licensee holds and hands back the licensor's Product data on termination, so the preferred data-export/deletion mechanic maps only loosely onto this genre. On its material terms the clause sits at or above the fallback. Two sub-elements short of the preferred wording, noted rather than flagged: (a) there is no express obligation on Array to return or destroy Ono Confidential Information and Data with a deletion certificate (14.2(a)(vi) is one-directional), which is better raised under the confidentiality rule; and (b) Article IX is not listed in the Section 14.5 survival provision, so supply continuity during the Wind-down Period is arguably unaddressed - that belongs to a supply/survival rule, not this insert. Neither is material to this rule's fallback, so no redline.
